author: difficulty44_author_h

source_artifacts.claim: The current authored room pairs counterweight lifts A/B, supplies a movable glucose sac and a central crossing shelf, places lethal slime below both shafts, and has no collectibles. The optional hint gives a route but is excluded from unassisted visible-clarity claims.
Players, crates, and active villains contribute weight; a rider is required on each deck, and the sign of load A minus load B determines opposite deck motion.
A non-heavy crate can be moved by one adjacent hero pressing toward it; pushing requires physical contact and can be blocked by solids.
The ordinary shared keyboard maps Isp to A/D/W and Pac to arrow left/right/up, confirming separate simultaneous controls without a dedicated counterweight command.
A boomerang hit gives Isp dizzy or Pac shove effects temporarily; this affects control execution but is not evidence of lethal harm.
Players can physically transfer velocity to active villains on contact, establishing an alternative source of body movement whose use as ballast still needs route confirmation.

prior_knowledge.concept: Movement, jumping, separate hero controls, and the both-matching-exits goal.

evidence.claim: The first campaign packet visibly presents the two control schemes, pad roles, and both-exits goal.

prior_knowledge.concept: A rider on each linked lift releases its clutch, and relative cargo/player weight can drive an opposite-deck exchange; the same board language and base mechanic appeared earlier, but the signal-sac crossing and unloading sequence are new here.

evidence.claim: Earlier board visibly repeats WAIT FOR BOTH, rider requirement, load feedback, and linked A/B direction; prior exposure is not assumed mastery.
Earlier authored room used paired counterweight decks with a cargo-weight objective, confirming this mechanic was practiced before position 41.

prior_knowledge.concept: Positioning and pushing an ordinary crate onto a surface to change its role as cargo/ballast.

evidence.claim: Earlier room introduction visibly teaches crate pushing and placement; applying a glucose sac as lift ballast in this layout is a transfer, not assumed mastery.

prior_knowledge.concept: Cana's boomerang can temporarily alter the heroes' control response; the exact Isp/Pac effects are visible in this room's board, while the consequences of being hit are not shown by the earlier packet.

evidence.claim: The earlier introduction describes Cana shoving Gem and Isp catching FLOAT, establishing prior boomerang interaction exposure.

prior_knowledge.concept: Delivering parcels or signal sacs between routes has been practiced; this room applies that transfer idea to a sac whose weight reverses linked counterweights.

evidence.claim: Earlier introduction explicitly asks players to deliver both parcels before reaching KEEP; exposure does not establish mastery of the current ballast transfer.

mechanics.fact: Both heroes must simultaneously be riders for the linked counterweights to move. Their body weights count 1 each; an ordinary crate counts 1. The larger loaded side moves down and the other up, to a 160-unit end stop.

evidence.claim: The implementation computes support closures, rider booleans, and direction from load difference; platform travel is bounded.
The idle capture visibly labels both riders on and shows A load 2 / B load 1 while A moves down and B up.

mechanics.fact: A workable route uses Pac plus the sac to load A while Isp rides B; at the shared far stop, Isp crosses via the upper signal fold while Pac pushes the sac across the commissure onto B, then Isp boards A. The heavier B load reverses the pair and carries both heroes toward their opposite docks; the sac can unload to Pac's lower dock.

evidence.claim: The recovery shelf catches an off-deck sac, the commissure is the shared crossing, and paired decks are defined.
The production route trace shows the crossing phase with heroes and cargo at the central transition; later route states show the exchange and return.
The production replay ends with both exits reached and the glucose sac on the lower-right dock.

mechanics.fact: The room has slime at the bottom of both lift shafts that harms either hero; falling into it is physically dangerous. The successful recorded route avoids it. Cana's boomerang can dizzy Isp or shove Pac temporarily, but this is a control disruption and not a lethal hazard by itself.

evidence.claim: Both shaft-floor hazards are slime and harm both heroes; no collectibles are authored.
Boomerang effects are temporary control effects.

mechanics.fact: A plausible physical-villain ballast alternative exists because active villains have weight 1 and players can push them, but no checked route establishes that a villain can replace the sac and still complete both exits; do not treat the sac as uniquely necessary.

evidence.claim: Active villain bodies count as ballast and rider requirements remain player-specific.
Physical player contact can impart velocity to an active villain body.

legal_routes.name: Recorded both-exit transfer (verified against current production LEVELS)

steps.goal: Get a rider on each deck and establish A heavier than B.
steps.action: Allow the spawn bodies to settle, then control Pac with right and Isp with left/jump as required to put Pac and the sac on A and Isp on B.
steps.expected_feedback: A load exceeds B, the panel moves from WAIT FOR BOTH to MOVING, A descends and B rises.
steps.observed_feedback: The production trace shows both riders, A load 2/B load 1 and the predicted direction; the 1687-frame current-source replay completes with no death.

evidence.claim: The trace has both riders and relative loads at the moving phase.
The independently repeated current-source schedule completes at frame 1687.

steps.goal: Reach the upper signal fold when decks align at the far stop.
steps.action: Jump from B to the fold while Pac stays with the sac on A.
steps.expected_feedback: Isp can cross above the commissure; Pac can push the light sac from A across to B.
steps.observed_feedback: The production trace records Isp on the upper fold while Pac and the sac transfer across the center; exact human timing and cue legibility are unmeasured.

evidence.claim: Trace shows the upper-fold crossing phase.
Fold, central commissure, and paired lifts form the authored crossing route.

steps.goal: Reverse the linked lifts after the sac changes sides, then split toward matching exits.
steps.action: Isp returns to A while Pac remains on B with the sac; ride the reversed exchange. At the far stop Isp traverses to the upper-left dock and Pac to the lower-right dock.
steps.expected_feedback: B is heavier, so B descends and A rises; Isp and Pac reach their own exits.
steps.observed_feedback: The main replay ends with both correct exits, zero deaths, and the sac on the right lower dock.

evidence.claim: Both exits are reached after the transfer; the sac is on the lower-right dock.
Upper-left and lower-right docks connect the moving platforms to player-matched exits.
The deterministic production route completes both exits in 1687 frames with zero deaths; it is evidence of route legality, not human difficulty.
Independent replay using current LEVELS also completed both exits without death.

The public production replay result identifies this route schedule as originating from tests/_temp/physical_level29_solver/jump_exit_inputs.json. That file is historical/private input provenance only; the replay result and current-source corroboration above are the outcome evidence.

steps.goal: Recover after a premature dismount from B.
steps.action: Reposition and jump back onto B while Isp stays on the other lift; continue the transfer route.
steps.expected_feedback: The rider condition resumes and the linked lift can continue; if the weight split is wrong, the pair may return to the prior stop rather than fail irreversibly.
steps.observed_feedback: The current-source replay completes both exits at frame 1699 with zero death, 12 frames beyond the main route.

evidence.claim: The retained recovery schedule dismounts/reboards Pac and still reaches both exits with no death.
Independent current-source recovery replay completes without death.
This specific missed-reboard slip is recoverable by reboarding and finishing the route.

isp: Must ride a deck during each counterweight movement; transfers between B, the upper fold, and A allow the central crossing and provide access to the upper-left matching exit.
Its route is affected by Cana's dizzy effect; exact exposure depends on timing and was not separately measured.
pac: Must ride the opposite deck, pushes the glucose sac from A across the commissure to B, and uses the lower-right dock/exit.
The sack's weight creates the intended load difference in the verified route, though villain-ballast alternatives remain untested.

common_mistakes.mistake: Dismounting from a lift before the partner has established a safe replacement state or before the intended reversal is ready.
common_mistakes.consequence: The rider condition can pause lift motion or let the wrong weight difference move the platforms toward the prior stop; the heroes are not automatically killed.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reboard the intended deck and restore the planned load split. The retained missed-reboard program completes with 12 additional simulated frames and zero deaths; this says nothing about human recovery time.

evidence.claim: Rider absence pauses motion; load difference controls direction.
A reboard recovery still completes both exits with zero deaths.

common_mistakes.mistake: Misreading a temporary shove/dizzy effect as a lift failure, or jumping into a slime-lined shaft while pursuing a missed transfer.
common_mistakes.consequence: Movement/jump control can be temporarily disrupted; falling to shaft-floor slime is lethal and can force a restart.
common_mistakes.recovery: Wait out temporary effect and regroup on the recovery shelf/deck; if a hero dies, the route's exact restart cost was not independently measured here. Do not assume the 12-frame reboard variant models death recovery.

evidence.claim: Boomerang hit causes temporary control effects.
Slime at the bottom of both shafts harms both heroes.

reasoning.rationale: The pair must reason about linked state, relative weight, a transferable crate, a center-crossing geometry, and the reversal order, so planning remains substantial even though the core two-rider rule was already introduced in level 23. The successful trace confirms one causal plan but does not prove uniqueness; physical villains can contribute weight, and no exhaustive alternative search was done. First-pass 3 remains appropriate: route evidence resolves uncertainty without removing the multi-step inference.

evidence.claim: Players, crates, and villains contribute weights; movement depends on both riders and relative load.
A complete transfer route exists, but one trace is not proof of a unique route.

cooperation.rationale: Two independent riders are a hard mechanical condition for lift motion, and the useful load split requires coordinated roles: Pac accompanies and pushes cargo while Isp crosses above and reboards. Neither hero is shown as a substitute for the other's matched exit. The score is not higher because the counterweight rule itself supports the joint action rather than requiring precise synchronized timing throughout.

evidence.claim: Both player-specific rider flags are required for motion.
Trace shows the sac on the opposite lift while heroes occupy separate route roles.

execution.rationale: The legal route requires separate movement/jump inputs, pushing a crate through a central crossing, and boarding narrow moving decks while avoiding lower shafts. The deterministic clear establishes feasibility, not human success or measured effort. First-pass null becomes 3 because the route and concrete geometry are now known; its remaining execution load is meaningful but not extreme by source evidence alone.

evidence.claim: Separate movement and jump inputs are required for the two heroes.
The sac must traverse recovery/crossing geometry among moving decks and fixed surfaces.
A scripted route finishes, confirming executable feasibility but not human performance.

timing.rationale: There is no authored deadline or timed hazard in the confirmed route. The lift moves continuously only while both riders remain aboard, so changing rider/load state is a timing consideration, but the route has no demonstrated narrow reaction window and can pause or reverse. First-pass null becomes low-but-nonzero to reflect state-dependent coordination, not a timed test.

evidence.claim: Lift motion depends on current rider/load state and is clamped to the endpoint; no deadline is defined.
The counterweight speed is set and hazards are static shaft floors, with no timed hazard definition.

hazards.rationale: The slime floors in both shafts are lethal, making an uncontrolled fall consequential. The verified route avoids them and no timed hazard or mandatory slime crossing is indicated, so physical danger is moderate rather than dominant. Temporary boomerang effects are treated separately as control friction, not as physical danger. First-pass null becomes 2 because source establishes actual danger and route avoidance.

evidence.claim: Both shaft-floor slime hazards harm both heroes.
The successful route records zero deaths while reaching both exits.

novelty.rationale: First-pass 3 treated the paired lift state as unfamiliar. Position 23 already visibly taught WAIT FOR BOTH, rider requirement, load display, and linked counterweights, so the underlying mechanic is previously practiced. New transfer lies in using a single sac as ballast across a brain-fold crossing, then reversing the pair for the exits; this is a moderate layout/causal transfer, not wholly new machinery.

evidence.claim: Earlier level visibly presents linked lifts, both riders, and load display.
The new transfer uses the sac and center crossing to exchange relative lift load.

recovery_cost.rationale: First-pass null becomes low for the observed/replayed boarding slip: a route variant dismounts Pac and reboards, then finishes both exits with zero deaths and only 12 additional simulated frames. A shaft fall or death may have a much larger restart cost; that consequence is not conflated with this cheap mistake and no exact death-recovery measurement is claimed.

evidence.claim: Missed-reboard variant completes with zero deaths and 12 more simulated frames than the main route.
Authored recovery shelf/floor offers a place to catch and push an off-deck sac back.

solution_clarity.rationale: The initial screenshot gives a strong rider condition and A/B direction/load feedback; the same visible grammar appeared in earlier position 23, lowering novelty. However, neither the screenshot nor source-proven route can establish that a first-time player will infer the sac's transfer and upper-fold crossing without using the optional hint. First-pass 3 is reduced to 2 because the board provides operational state cues and a closely matching earlier lesson, while the multi-step transfer remains implicit.

evidence.claim: The current board explicitly says WAIT FOR BOTH, rider-on-each-deck releases the clutch, and displays the upper/lower stops.
Earlier visual teaching uses the same board rule and linked lift state.

control_friction.rationale: Unknown: the cited key mapping and scripted/native route evidence establish technical feasibility, but do not verify shared-keyboard two-human input reliability or a control defect. No browser keyboard-event reliability evidence is cited. Plausible risk only: Boarding/transfer coordination belongs to execution; temporary boomerang response effects are intentional and belong to execution.

evidence.claim: The packet displays A/D/W for Isp and arrow keys for Pac.
The runtime maps separate movement/jump keys to the heroes.
Temporary boomerang effects can alter movement response.

confidence_reason: Current source and two production LEVELS replays confirm a complete main route and one recovery, and source definitions establish weights, hazards, input mapping, and physical alternatives. Confidence remains medium because this is not a fresh44 playtest, alternative ballast routes were not exhaustively tested, visible cues do not prove first-time inference, and no human effort/control observations exist.

confirmed: The visible instruction that a rider on each deck releases the clutch is mechanically accurate; current source confirms that both rider flags gate movement.
The A-down/B-up and end-stop labels match the relative-load rule and bounded travel.
Both matching exits are mandatory; the recorded route reaches both.
missed_mechanics: The load display is causal: heavier A moves A down/B up, and moving the sac to B reverses the pair.
The glucose sac is ordinary pushable ballast in the verified route, and the upper fold/commissure create the transfer crossing.
Both lower shafts contain lethal slime, while Cana's boomerang produces temporary control effects rather than direct damage.
A missed boarding can be recovered, and the route has a catch shelf for the sac.
incorrect_inferences: None of the first-pass hypotheses was asserted as an observed fact; they remain appropriate uncertainties for that evidence boundary.
changed_judgments: Execution changed from null to 3 because a concrete legal route now demonstrates the movement/jump/push/boarding demands, while still not predicting human success.
Timing changed from null to 1 because rider/load state continuously determines motion but the pair can pause/reverse and there is no deadline or demonstrated narrow window.
Hazards changed from null to 2 because source identifies lethal slime floors, and the verified route avoids them.
Novelty decreased from 3 to 2 because level 23 previously introduced/practiced the same paired-lift rider/load rule; the new work is the sac transfer and reversal route.
Recovery cost changed from null to 1 for the specific reboarding mistake supported by a zero-death replay, not for death/restart outcomes.
Solution clarity decreased from 3 to 2 because current and prior boards expose rider/load/direction cues, though the transfer plan remains implicit and optional hints are excluded.

At 2026-10-17T17:51:21Z, the paired control-friction estimate was withdrawn from 2 to unknown: available source mappings and scripted/native input traces establish feasibility, not shared-keyboard two-human input reliability or control failure. Plausible coordination, execution, and intentional movement-effect concerns remain qualitative risks in their own dimensions.
unresolved: Whether active villains can replace the glucose sac as sufficient ballast and still permit both exits; source makes this plausible, but no route was tested.
Whether a novice will infer the sac transfer/central crossing without the optional hint; no human play was observed.
Exact death/restart or fall recovery cost, including whether reset returns to this room or restarts a broader sequence.
Actual human timing, execution success, control reliability, fun, comfort, and first-encounter difficulty.
Whether the production replay route schedule is intuitive or merely one deterministic solution; route existence does not establish route uniqueness or usability.

single_operator_note: The baseline assumes two people, one for each hero. One operator would have to alternate or overlap A/D/W and arrow inputs, including coordinating the central crossing, crate push, boarding, and exit split; that additional attention/multitasking demand is not folded into the two-human ratings.
